AUTHOR: Park
TITLE: A Study on Enhancement of Fish Recognition Using Cumulative Mean of YOLO Network in Underwater Video Images
VENUE: JOURNAL OF MARINE SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING
SPECIES: Largemouth bass, Bluegill, Common carp, Crucian carp, Catfish, Mandarin fish, Skin carp (test only bass and bluegill)
DATA: Own: training images captured in laboratory (5000 per species); test videos from installed underwater photography system in a pond
V_EV: Sec. 2.2/4: 'Since there are many floats in the aquatic environment, the video image changes according to the change of sun and external light.'
D2: training = lab images; test = separate pond videos
D_EV: Sec. 2.2/4: 'video images of fish were taken directly in the laboratory environment'; 'The Largemouth bass and the Bluegill video images taken in the pond were used for the performance evaluation.'
R_EV: Sec. 4: 'The Largemouth bass and the Bluegill video images taken in the pond were used for the performance evaluation.' (model trained on laboratory images)
E_EV: Sec. 4: 'recognizes 62 (which is 93.94%) of a total of 66 fish as Bluegill, and did not classify 4 Bluegills'; 'can accurately count the population of fish.'
ARCH: YOLOv2 (MATLAB) + cumulative-mean heuristic over frames, capture-line counting
METR: AP per species (training), classification/recognition rate of individual fish in test videos
NOTE: INCL uncertain: test videos from an 'installed underwater photography system' in a 'pond' — not stated whether natural or aquaculture pond; included as fixed-camera field deployment in freshwater. Training data captured in laboratory, so lab->pond treated as external (water/camera change); in-domain figure is only YOLO 'learning results' AP (unclear if held-out), so R3=N. Text heavily scrambled by pdftotext overlay. Counting = number of individual fish correctly classified vs true number in test videos (34 bass, 66 bluegill); missed fish reported (4 bluegills not classified) -> E4=FNR. '60% or greater' is a description of observed probabilities, not a stated threshold.
